messages:
support-jen: @sre-oncall FYI Velociti just opened a P1 — their customers seeing intermittent 504s and a lot of tail latency on hosted inference (p99 ~6s). sample req id: vel-req-8a3f. They say failures started ~20:50 UTC and are ongoing.

sre-oncall: thanks. which region and model? any recent deploys?

support-jen: us-west-2, model: redwood-open-13b-quant, traffic spike from a batch import job. No deploys from our side in the last 3 hours. customer says requests hang then get `504 gateway timeout`.

ops-bot: ALERT: ingress_queue_depth(us-west-2) = 1286 (> 1000 threshold). Continuous-batcher backlog increasing.

miran: putting this on my queue. initial hypothesis: continuous-batcher backlog + KV cache churn = long dequeue times. Are we seeing early reject logs (`queue_depth_exceeded`)?

sre-oncall: pulling logs now.

sre-oncall: snippet from ingress logs for vel-req-8a3f: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-17T20:51:12Z","req_id":"vel-req-8a3f","msg":"enqueue","queue_depth":1204} \n{"ts":"2026-03-17T20:51:18Z","req_id":"vel-req-8a3f","msg":"dequeue_start","dequeue_delay_ms":6010} \n{"ts":"2026-03-17T20:51:18Z","req_id":"vel-req-8a3f","msg":"error","err":"upstream 504: deadline exceeded"}```

elaine: looks like p99 dequeue_delay > 6s. That matches the customer's tail timeouts. Is batching policy too aggressive?

miran: two things to check: 1) queue depth limit is 1250 for that pool (older config), 2) continuous batching has a max_batch_delay that can cause head-of-line blocking for long seq requests. The KV cache cold starts can cause some tokens to take 2-3x longer.

support-jen: customer says their import job sent many long-context requests (seq_len ~8k tokens). Could that be causing batcher stalls?

miran: yes. long-seq requests blow up kernel execution and hold GPU slots while other requests queue. We should get a repro: ask customer to share a small reproducer with one long seq that triggers a stalled batch. Meanwhile, mitigation options: - enable small-request-priority policy - route long-seq traffic to a slower but dedicated pool - temporarily increase queue depth/shrinking max_batch_size.

sre-oncall: trying a config change in staging to shrink max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 and enable small-request-priority. If staging is good I'll push to canary in us-west-2.

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: applied canary config to pool us-west-2-cpu-1 (shrink batch size). Monitoring for 10 minutes.

sre-oncall: after canary deploy p99 dequeue_delay dropped from 6.2s -> 1.1s for small requests; large seq still slow but fewer head-of-line timeouts. Customer reports error rate dropping from 14% -> 3%.

customer-ops: We still see ~1 in 200 requests time out when long sequences hit. Is there a short-term routing we can do?

miran: yes. immediate short-term: route long-seq label to dedicated pool (velociti-dedicated) or set per-tenant max_concurrent_longseq=2. Long-term: add admission control that throttles long-seq while preserving short-request latency.

elaine: also flag for product: consider model variant with kv-cache prewarm for long-document ingestion flows.

sre-oncall: a few actionable repro steps for support to coordinate with customer: 1) reproduce with curl: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \\n -H "X-Custom-Tenant: velociti" \\n -d '{"model":"redwood-open-13b-quant","input":"<~8k tokens payload>","stream":false}'
``` 2) Add header `X-Debug-Req: 1` to capture ingress timing. 3) Provide two sample req_ids that timed out.

support-jen: relayed to Velociti; they will run the curl and send back samples.

ops-bot: MONITOR: queue_depth dropping to 420 after canary; error rate trending down.

customer-ops: sending two sample ids: vel-req-8a3f (from earlier) and vel-req-8b44. Attached brief stack capture.

sre-oncall: thx. captured full trace shows dequeue_delay spike due to a single large batch with 1x long-seq: ```
BatchID: b-20260317-507
members: 63 (62 short, 1 long)
processing_time_ms: 7200
long_seq_member: vel-req-8a3f
```

miran: confirmed head-of-line blocking. Next steps: 1) set admission control to reject if queue_depth>1400 and long_seq_present in head, 2) prioritize short requests when batch contains mix, 3) schedule a follow-up to add per-tenant long-seq routing.

elaine: support notes for customer response: explain what we changed (canary reduced batch size + small-request-priority), recommend short-term routing to dedicated pool or rate-limit long import jobs, and invite them for a joint runbook session to implement per-tenant settings.

support-jen: customer happy to do runbook session tomorrow. I'll keep monitoring.

sre-oncall: marking mitigated for now. creating follow-up ticket to add auto-admission control + per-tenant long-seq protections.

miran: capturing logs and adding a small test-case in our regression suite so future continuous-batcher changes don't regress.

support-jen: closing thread once post-mortem note is added. :white_check_mark:
